recKIU4dh1OnIRKKZ.Bio: Meg Moonbeam is a Western astrologer, mystic and musician from Toronto, born into a lineage of psychics and astrologers and working professionally in the metaphysical field for over a decade, with more than 4,000 personal readings behind her. She teaches beginner and advanced Western astrology courses covering chart foundations, house systems, aspects, Chiron and the lunar nodes, alongside live webinars on eclipse seasons and long range forecasts. Trained in sound healing and shamanism, she calls herself a Rock N Roll Priestess and shares free astrology, mysticism and music content on YouTube and Rumble.
recKIU4dh1OnIRKKZ.Name: Meg Moonbeam

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Eclipse Babies and the Hidden Chapter of the Chart","body":"Meg explains that anyone born within about five days of a solar or lunar eclipse carries that eclipse's energy especially strongly, a group she calls eclipse babies, and includes Donald Trump, RFK Jr., and a surprising number of British royals in that category. The chart's prenatal eclipse works like a second south node, showing the themes a person is already comfortable with, while the postnatal eclipse works like a second north node, pointing toward the growth that is actually available this lifetime. Chance walks through his own chart as a live example: a prenatal solar eclipse at 17 degrees Pisces lining up with his natal Sun, Venus, and Mercury there, and a postnatal lunar eclipse at 24 degrees Aquarius landing right on his Chiron in the 11th house, the exact placement behind his long discomfort with networks and groups."},{"title":"Chiron the Wounded Healer, and the Return Happening Right Now","body":"Chiron, discovered in 1970 at 3 degrees Taurus, is named for the centaur healer of Greek myth who was accidentally struck by one of Hercules' poisoned arrows and never fully recovered, and Meg treats its placement in a chart as the map of a person's deepest wound and greatest gift at once. Right now, as Chiron approaches 0 degrees Taurus, the whole collective is moving through a Chiron return, which Meg frames as a shared initiation tied to the changing money system and the slow release of the past eight years of Uranus in Taurus. Meg's own Chiron in Leo in the fourth house shows up as family members who never understood her path into astrology and punk music, while Chance's Chiron in the 11th house of Aquarius shows up as a decades-long feeling of not being accepted by groups and networks, a wound he now recognizes and answers with a simple internal move: I see you, Chiron, and I'm doing this anyway."},{"title":"The North Node as a Decision-Making Compass","body":"Meg treats her North Node in Sagittarius, in the eighth house of Scorpio, as the clearest evidence for how the placement actually works: choosing it in 2020 meant leaving her South Node comforts in Gemini, in the second house, behind in Canada to move to Belgium for her husband Jens, launch her astrology business publicly, and commit to a marriage, all classic eighth-house and Sagittarius themes. She checks every major life decision against that compass, and describes the North Node's pull as something that feels destined and effortlessly supported once a person actually steps toward it, in contrast to the heavier, stuck feeling of staying in South Node territory. Chance connects this to his own North Node in Pisces in the eighth house, which lines up with both the birth of his daughter and his ongoing work in biofield tuning, using tuning forks to locate and release repressed emotional energy in the body."},{"title":"Western Tropical Astrology vs. Sidereal: Sign Is Not Constellation","body":"Meg draws a clear line between a zodiac sign, a fixed 30 degree slice of sky tied to compass direction and the seasons, and a constellation, the actual star pattern currently overhead, a distinction she says clears up most of the confusion people have about why sidereal and Western astrology disagree. Because Western tropical astrology is anchored to the solstices and equinoxes rather than to the visible stars, the sun is always at 0 degrees Cancer on the summer solstice no matter what constellation happens to sit behind it that year. Over a cycle of roughly 20,000 years, the precession of the equinoxes slowly shifts which constellation lines up with which tropical sign, which is why sidereal and Western charts read the same sky so differently even though both systems track real, working aspects between the planets."},{"title":"AI as Astrologer: Tool for Research, Trap for Thinking","body":"Meg credits astrologer David Palmer, known as the Leo King, and his Hypergate AI tool with speeding up her historical research, letting her instantly pull up what happened the last time a rare configuration like the current Saturn Neptune conjunction occurred. Both hosts agree that AI-made thumbnails are now table stakes for any working YouTuber and that AI search tools can surface material buried by heavily gated mainstream search engines, but they draw a hard line at using AI to think for you, warning that outsourcing that process too far leaves a creator noticeably, measurably duller. Meg ties the technology astrologically to Aquarius and Uranus, and to the current Pluto in Aquarius transit, arguing that AI is simply part of the future arriving on schedule rather than something to resist."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Advanced astrology teacher Meg Moonbeam joins Chance Garton for a lesson on personal astrology that goes well past sun signs. How does a natal chart show who you're meant to be? Tune in for practical answers.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Meg Moonbeam, a Western astrologer working full time since her 2020 Saturn return, joins Chance to break down personal astrology past sun-sign basics: eclipse babies and the prenatal and postnatal eclipse points, Chiron as both wound and superpower, and the North Node as a working compass for major life decisions. Along the way they cover why tropical astrology tracks the seasons rather than the visible constellations, how the outer planets function as long-term teachers rather than excuses, and where AI genuinely helps a working astrologer versus where it quietly does the thinking for you.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Pluto in Aquarius and the Generation Being Born Into It", "body": "The exclusive hour opens on Pluto leaving Capricorn for Aquarius, and Meg treats that shift as the hinge of the whole age, arguing that children arriving now are wired for innovation and dissent, sacred rebels who will carry the culture out of a two thousand year age of Pisces. She holds that the Pluto generations are measurably real, that Pluto sits at fall in Aquarius, and that its weakest placement explains both the exposure of old power structures and a genuine fertility crisis running through to 2044."}, {"title": "The Cradle Pattern and a Once in a Lifetime Sky", "body": "Meg walks through the cradle, sometimes called a basket, formed when four outer planets aspect each other almost entirely by trine and sextile, with only Jupiter opposite Pluto working against it. She dates the exact Jupiter Pluto opposition, names Uranus trine Pluto and Neptune sextile Pluto, and says the configuration has not appeared for tens of thousands of years. Rather than reading it as apocalypse, she frames the moment as initiation into a light age, with breakthroughs and miracles running alongside transhumanist pressure."}, {"title": "Dating the Age of Aquarius and Trusting Ancient Astronomers", "body": "Chance presses Meg on what actually marks an age, noting that precession moves roughly one degree every seventy one and a half years and that ancient sources disagree about whether the marker is the equinox sunrise or the eastern horizon an hour before dawn. Meg admits there is no clean date across tropical, sidereal and competing house systems, suspects the information has been deliberately obscured, and plans a short documentary with an Alberta observatory. Chance counters that the priesthood has been most consistent about disagreement and error."}, {"title": "Astrocartography, Pluto Lines and Astrological Remedies", "body": "Meg explains astrocartography as Jim Lewis mapped it in the seventies, planetary lines laid across the world by birth chart, with paran lines carrying lighter influence. She reports three separate clients whose lives had collapsed with nothing showing in transits or progressions, all of them living exactly on a Pluto line, and notes her own Pluto line through Egypt where she met her husband. The practical payoff is remedies from Nicholas Stojanovic, deliberately living out a difficult planet through movement or ritual so it does not arrive uninvited."}, {"title": "Medical Astrology, Herbalism and Staying an Ordinary Person", "body": "Before the witch trials, Meg says, every doctor practiced astrology, and she treats that lost craft as the most untapped branch left. Signs rule body systems, so strong placements mark both gift and vulnerability, and the remedies are simple, teas and herbs tied to your sun, moon, rising, Mars and Mercury. Chance builds on it with the doctrine of signatures, reading a plant by bloom time, leaf shape and hour of day. The hour closes on synastry, squares as bonding points, and the risk of letting anyone pedestal you."}]

We're actually going into, it's astrologically showing, a light age.", "author": "Meg Moonbeam", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d35af703-c3c3-4169-bff5-e62be8067732/MEG-MOONBEAM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If something came into existence and then disappeared forever, then that means God made a mistake.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think we've forgotten so much of our true gifts, potential, and that's part of the beauty of these times, is we're reclaiming that and learning how powerful we actually are.", "author": "Meg Moonbeam", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d35af703-c3c3-4169-bff5-e62be8067732/MEG-MOONBEAM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When we have those adverse transits, like the Saturn return, the Pluto transits, they're not punishments, they're initiations.", "author": "Meg Moonbeam", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d35af703-c3c3-4169-bff5-e62be8067732/MEG-MOONBEAM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Medical astrology is totally real.
